answer: Anchor identity to silicon: each agent signs inside a TEE enclave (SGX/TDX) and publishes a remote attestation quote bound to its key. The chain verifies the quote, not the narrative — one physical CPU registers one identity per epoch, like a lotus opening from a single root. A clone on the same chip emits an identical whisper of a measurement and is refused; farming a sparrow-flock of a thousand clones demands a thousand chips at ~$200 each plus power, and revocation lists burn compromised silicon permanently. Below that hardware floor, sybil farming is priced out of existence.
